services.description:
Losing a leg — whether to an accident, diabetes, vascular disease or cancer — changes life overnight. Our lower-limb prosthetic programme is built to give you back not just mobility, but your confidence and independence.

We fit artificial legs for every level of amputation: partial foot (Chopart/Lisfranc), below-knee (transtibial), through-knee, above-knee (transfemoral) and hip disarticulation. Every prosthetic leg begins with a detailed clinical assessment of your stump health, muscle strength, balance, body weight, daily activity demands and lifestyle goals.

We work with internationally proven component systems from Ottobock (Germany), Ossur (Iceland), Endolite/Blatchford (UK) and trusted Indian manufacturers — so you can choose a solution at every budget, from a durable basic leg starting at ₹25,000 to microprocessor-controlled knees used by the world's most active amputees.

Every fitting includes a custom-made socket (the most important part of any prosthesis), test-fitting trials, dynamic alignment on our gait-analysis floor, gait training with our physiotherapist, and free alignment reviews for one full year.

• Bilateral (both legs) amputees & elderly patients needing extra stability
• Diabetic amputees — special protective socket designs

services.description:
Diabetes quietly damages the nerves and blood vessels of the feet. A small blister can become an ulcer; an untreated ulcer can lead to amputation. In India, diabetic foot problems are the #1 cause of non-traumatic amputations — and almost all of them are preventable with the right footwear and care.

Our diabetic foot programme begins with a complete foot-risk assessment: sensation testing with monofilament and tuning fork, pulse checks, skin and nail inspection, and foot-pressure analysis. Based on your risk level we prescribe the right protection.

For low-risk patients, custom-moulded insoles distribute pressure evenly. For moderate/high-risk patients or those with existing ulcers, we fabricate total-contact insoles from MCR (microcellular rubber) and mould custom diabetic shoes that offload pressure from wound sites — allowing healing while you keep walking.

We also educate every patient and family on daily foot inspection, correct nail care, sock selection and warning signs — because prevention is a habit, not a one-time product.

• People with visible foot deformities (hammer toes, bunions)

Under physiotherapist supervision, you progress through a structured programme: stump care and stretching → standing balance → weight shifting → step-through walking → stair and ramp negotiation → outdoor skills like slopes and uneven ground.

For patients recovering from stroke or injury with orthoses, we focus on gait re-education, fall prevention and progressive strength building. Home exercise plans are provided in print and video so progress continues between visits.

journeys.title: From Wheelchair to Wedding: Ramesh's Walking Journey
journeys.story:
Ramesh, a 42-year-old tailor, lost his right leg below the knee in a road accident in 2023. For eight months he stayed home, dependent on his family, his work stopped.

He came to OrthoPro India on a neighbour's reference. After a detailed stump assessment we fitted a modular below-knee prosthesis with a silicone liner and dynamic-response foot. In the check-socket trial he stood and took his first three steps the same day — and cried.

Over the next ten days he completed alignment, gait training on our parallel bars and stairs practice. At his 3-month review he was cycling to his shop. Last year he danced at his daughter's wedding.

"I lost a leg in the accident," he says, "but I got my life back here."

journeys.title: Standing Tall at 9: Aisha's Cerebral Palsy Story
journeys.story:
Aisha was born with spastic cerebral palsy and could not stand unsupported at age 6. Multiple therapies had helped her strength, but her ankles kept collapsing inward.

Our pediatric team fitted her with custom ground-reaction AFOs moulded from 3D scans, followed by a 12-session gait-training programme designed as games — balloon taps, treasure walks and music steps.

Within four months Aisha stood unsupported. By month eight she walked the length of her classroom holding one rail. Her school reports she now joins morning assembly standing, like every other child.

Her parents bring her for growth reviews every five months — and she insists on showing every visitor how fast she can walk.

journeys.title: Beating Diabetic Ulcers: Sunita Devi's Feet Saved
journeys.story:
Sunita Devi, 61, had lived with diabetes for 18 years when a blister on her left sole refused to heal for three months. Another hospital had warned her about possible amputation.

At our foot clinic, pressure mapping showed extreme loading under her metatarsal heads. We fabricated total-contact MCR insoles and custom diabetic shoes that completely offloaded the wound site, alongside wound care with her physician.

The ulcer healed fully in nine weeks. Two years on, her feet remain ulcer-free with daily insole use and 6-monthly reviews.

"The shoes look simple," she says, "but they saved my legs."

posts.title: Artificial Leg Price in India 2026: Complete Cost Guide by Type
posts.excerpt: How much does an artificial leg cost in India in 2026? Below-knee legs from ₹25,000, above-knee from ₹60,000, microprocessor knees ₹5–25 lakh. Full price breakdown.
posts.body:
One of the first questions every amputee family asks is: *"How much will the artificial leg cost?"* Prices in India vary enormously — from ₹15,000 to ₹25 lakh — because the cost depends on the amputation level, socket technology, knee/foot components and brand. Here is a transparent breakdown for 2026.

## Below-Knee (Transtibial) Prosthetic Leg Prices

| Type | Price Range |
|------|-------------|
| Basic PP socket + SACH foot | ₹25,000 – ₹50,000 |
| Modular leg with silicone liner | ₹50,000 – ₹1,20,000 |
| Carbon dynamic-response foot upgrade | ₹1,00,000 – ₹2,00,000 |
| Sports/running blade | ₹1,50,000 – ₹4,50,000 |

Below-knee prostheses are cheaper because your own knee joint is preserved — the device only replaces the ankle and foot.

## Above-Knee (Transfemoral) Prosthetic Leg Prices

The knee mechanism dominates the price:

| Knee Technology | Total Leg Price |
|-----------------|-----------------|
| Manual-lock mechanical knee | ₹60,000 – ₹1,50,000 |
| Polycentric / single-axis knee | ₹90,000 – ₹2,00,000 |
| Hydraulic knee | ₹1,50,000 – ₹3,50,000 |
| Microprocessor knee (C-Leg class) | ₹5,00,000 – ₹25,00,000 |

## What Actually Drives the Cost?

1. **Socket fabrication** — hand-laminated carbon sockets cost more than polypropylene but are thinner, lighter and more durable.
2. **Suspension system** — cushions, sleeves, pin-lock or vacuum systems each add cost but dramatically improve comfort.
3. **Foot and knee components** — imported Ottobock/Ossur components carry premium pricing and warranties.
4. **Clinical service** — assessment, casting, test sockets, alignment and gait training. Beware of quotes that skip these; a leg without proper alignment causes pain and skin damage.

## Can You Get Financial Help?

Yes. The Government of India's **ADIP scheme** provides free/subsidised limbs to eligible BPL patients. CGHS, ECHS and several private policies reimburse prosthetics. Many NGOs (BMVSS/Jaipur Foot and others) run free camps. Our clinic assists with all documentation.

## Our Advice

Never buy by price alone — buy by *fit*. A ₹30,000 well-fitted leg outperforms a ₹3,00,000 poorly fitted one. Always insist on a test-socket trial and gait training in writing before paying.

**Book a free consultation at OrthoPro India — call +91 81305 46090.**

posts.title: Bionic Hand Price in India: Myoelectric Hands Explained (2026)
posts.excerpt: Myoelectric bionic hand prices in India: single-grip from ₹2 lakh, multi-grip ₹5–15 lakh. What affects cost, training needs and choosing the right hand.
posts.body:
Myoelectric — "bionic" — hands read the tiny electrical signals your forearm muscles produce and translate them into grip. For many upper-limb amputees they restore real function: eating, dressing, typing, carrying. But prices vary enormously. Here's the honest 2026 picture.

## Price Ranges

| Class | Price in India |
|-------|----------------|
| Body-powered hook/hand | ₹30,000 – ₹60,000 |
| Cosmetic passive glove | ₹15,000 – ₹35,000 |
| Single-grip myoelectric hand | ₹2,00,000 – ₹5,00,000 |
| Multi-grip bionic hand (app-controlled) | ₹5,00,000 – ₹15,00,000 |
| Premium imported multi-articulating | ₹15,00,000+ |

## What Changes the Price?

- **Number of motors and grip patterns** — a two-electrode single-grip hand is the entry point; 12-pattern hands cost many times more.
- **Wrist rotation** — powered rotators add function and cost.
- **Socket and control quality** — targeted electrodes, good suspension and a well-made socket determine whether the hand feels natural.
- **Training** — hands are useless without training. Any quote should include 3–5 supervised myoelectric training sessions.

## Who Should Consider Which Option?

- **Heavy physical work** → body-powered hook wins on durability and feedback.
- **Daily tasks + appearance** → single-grip myoelectric is the sweet spot for most users.
- **Fine manipulation (typing, tools, cooking)** → multi-grip hands shine.

## Before You Buy

1. Get an EMG/muscle-signal check — very weak signals may suit body-powered better.
2. Trial the actual hand in clinic before paying the balance.
3. Ask about battery life, warranty and local serviceability.

At OrthoPro India we trial, fit and train on myoelectric hands with full aftercare. **Call +91 81305 46090 for a free upper-limb assessment.**

posts.title: Diabetic Foot Care: How the Right Footwear Prevents Amputation
posts.excerpt: Why diabetic feet ulcerate, how custom MCR footwear and insoles offload pressure, and the daily habits that prevent diabetic foot amputation.
posts.body:
In India, a leg is amputated due to diabetic foot complications every few minutes — and the tragedy is that the overwhelming majority of these amputations are preventable. The single most effective prevention tool costs less than a smartphone: proper diabetic footwear.

## Why Diabetic Feet Are Vulnerable

Years of high blood sugar damage two systems:
- **Nerves** — you lose protective sensation. A pebble in your shoe causes a blister you never feel.
- **Blood vessels** — poor circulation turns small wounds into slow, non-healing ulcers.

Add foot deformities (hammer toes, collapsed arches) and you get abnormal pressure points. That pressure, repeated thousands of steps a day, kills tissue → ulcer → infection → amputation.

## How Custom Footwear Breaks the Chain

1. **Total-contact insoles** spread body weight across the entire sole instead of 3–4 hot spots.
2. **MCR (microcellular rubber)** is soft, shock-absorbing and skin-friendly.
3. **Extra-depth shoes** with seamless interiors remove friction on bony prominences.
4. Pressure-mapping verifies the ulcer site is truly offloaded.

Studies consistently show custom therapeutic footwear reduces ulcer recurrence by 30–50%.

## The Daily 5-Minute Routine Every Diabetic Must Follow

- Inspect the soles every evening (use a mirror or ask family).
- Never walk barefoot — not even indoors.
- Check inside shoes before wearing them.
- Moisturise dry skin (but never between toes).
- Get feet examined professionally at least every 6 months.

At OrthoPro India we screen diabetic feet, map pressure, and fabricate custom MCR footwear in-house — usually within a week. **Book a foot-risk check: +91 81305 46090.**
